title: The Ad That Paid For Decades
why_movie: RESULT: a $35 mail-order ad, re-run word for word, turned into royalty deals that paid him for decades - he says it was 'almost like I had a trust fund with a million dollars a year coming in.' METHOD: he says an energetic 'money process' his mentor ran on him cleared a block in his field - no copy change, same ad, different result. WISH: a stranger with a side hustle going nowhere would want the 14 audios after hearing the exact same effort suddenly pay off once something unseen was cleared.
keep: Good. You have to pay me
I'm going to go back and try this direct mail piece again
Every day, I would get cash
All because one process was run

scenes.on: I have a report. If you'd like to buy the report, it's $35.
scenes.gen: A 1970s kitchen table at night, a single typed one-page report under a lamp beside a stack of blank order-form envelopes and a rotary phone
scenes.move: a hand slides the one-page report into a plain envelope and seals it

scenes.on: No orders and I was out several thousand dollars.
scenes.gen: A young man in a 1970s collared shirt at a small table in a dim apartment at dusk, sorting a stack of opened envelopes that are all empty, cold blue light from the window
scenes.move: he flips through the mail and lets the last empty envelope fall onto the table

scenes.on: I have a block. It's like there's like a black cloud. It's an energetic block.
scenes.gen: A young man in a 1970s collared shirt sits across a wooden desk from an older bearded mentor in a dark study at night, thick candle smoke curling in a shaft of moonlight above the young man's shoulder
scenes.move: the smoke slowly curls and thickens in the moonlight above the young man's shoulder

scenes.on: Would you like to have it released?
scenes.gen: Close view of an older bearded mentor in a dark candlelit study raising one open hand, a brass bowl of glowing embers on the desk, haze drifting in a beam of blue moonlight
scenes.move: the mentor slowly raises his open hand as the haze drifts through the moonlight

scenes.on: Good. You have to pay me. And back then, one money process that he offered me was like $5,000 back in 1979.
scenes.gen: A young man's hands counting worn hundred dollar bills into a stack on a dark wooden desk under a warm brass lamp, an older man's open hand waiting on the table
scenes.move: the hand places the last bill on the stack and slides it across the desk

scenes.on: I'm going to go back and try this direct mail piece again.
scenes.gen: A cramped 1970s print shop at night, a typeset block of the same newspaper advertisement sitting unchanged under a bright work lamp on a metal table
scenes.move: a man's hand taps the unchanged typeset block once and pulls back

scenes.on: Every day, I would get cash and money orders for $35. One, two, three, four, five, ten, $350. $1,000 a day was pouring in.
scenes.gen: A cramped 1970s home office at night, a desk completely buried under a growing pile of opened envelopes with loose cash and money orders spilling onto the floor
scenes.move: more envelopes slide off the overflowing desk pile and scatter across the floor

scenes.on: They would pay me royalties and I would get residual income, royalty income for decades later, which allowed me the freedom to travel the world, do what I wanted, it was almost like I had a trust fund with a million dollars a year coming in.
scenes.gen: A young man driving a cream colored convertible along a sunny coastal highway at golden hour, relaxed with one hand on the wheel, open ocean on one side
scenes.move: the convertible cruises steadily along the coastal road as the camera tracks alongside it

payoff: one process was run, one energetic block was released
caption:
Comment "WISH" and I'll send you Kevin Trudeau's 14 Your Wish Is Your Command audios. Free.

Kevin Trudeau says he once ran a mail-order ad for a $35 report. He spent money on the ad and the printing, and for a month nothing came back. He was out several thousand dollars.

He told his mentor what happened. His mentor looked and said there was a block in his field, and asked if he wanted it released - but it would cost him.

He paid it. Then he ran the exact same ad, word for word, no changes. What came back this time, and for how many years, is the part you have to hear from him.

{episode}

The 14 audios are Kevin teaching how to use your mind to get what you want in life. They were recorded live at a private event in the Alps.

Most people will watch this and scroll on. A few will comment "WISH" and start listening tonight.

No message within a minute? Look in your message requests, or use the link in my bio.
